title: Single-cell analysis protocol for studying heterogeneity in cultured mammalian cells
author: Chen, Ozturk, et al.
materials: Chromium Chip B Single Cell Kit

We also provide a user-friendly notebook interface to automate the computational analyses, making them easy to apply to any scRNAseq data. Implementing multi-step bioinformatic pipelines for data processing and analysis can represent a barrier for reproducing analyses or applying them to new data sets. To address this, our computational workflows are encoded in GenePattern notebooks that provide well-documented and easily modifiable code. Furthermore, these notebooks can be run locally or online via the GenePattern server and are self-contained such that users do not need to install dependencies or third party software. New users can ensure understanding and reproducibility by running our dataset on the GenePattern notebooks as a test case.

steps.title: Digest gel and prepare single cells
steps.instruction: Process the collagen gel to obtain a single‑cell suspension suitable for FACS while preserving transcriptional signatures.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the collagen gel to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 50 µL of 10 mg/mL collagenase to the gel.
Gently mash the gel with a P1000 pipette tip to mechanically disrupt it.
Incubate the gel in a 37 °C water bath for 5 min.
Pipette the entire solution up and down with the P1000 tip, minimizing bubbles.
Incubate again at 37 °C for 5 min.
Mix the solution with a P200 tip, again pipetting up and down while avoiding bubbles.
Incubate a third time at 37 °C for 5 min.
Centrifuge the suspension at 400 × g for 4 min.
Discard the supernatant, add 50 µL of 0.25 % trypsin, and resuspend the pellet.
Incubate at 37 °C for 5 min.
Mix the solution with a P200 tip.
Incubate at 37 °C for another 5 min.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 4 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in ice‑cold FACS buffer.
Strain the cells prior to sorting.
Use forward‑ and side‑scatter density plots to exclude debris.
Set red‑fluorescence gates using un‑photoconverted control cells.
Collect cells that display red fluorescence above the gate.

steps.title: Perform differential expression analysis
steps.instruction: Identify cluster‑specific markers and generate a heatmap of differentially expressed genes.

substeps.instruction: Apply the DESeq2 algorithm to identify positive and negative markers for each cluster or phenotype.
Correct for multiple testing using the Benjamini & Hochberg method.
Select genes with an adjusted p‑value lower than 0.05 as differentially expressed.
Generate an expression heatmap to visualize differential expression across clusters.

steps.title: Conduct GO term over‑representation analysis
steps.instruction: Find enriched Gene Ontology biological processes among positive markers.

substeps.instruction: Submit the list of positive‑marker genes to the PANTHER classification system, choosing Homo sapiens as the reference organism and the GO biological process complete annotation set.
Select Fisher’s Exact test and apply Benjamini & Hochberg correction; retain terms with FDR < 0.05.
Export gene‑set statistics (p‑values, sizes, overlapping counts) from PANTHER, import them into Python, and create a bar plot ranking gene sets by p‑value.

steps.title: Run pseudotime trajectory analysis
steps.instruction: Infer cellular progression using Monocle3 and visualize it on UMAP plots.

substeps.instruction: Convert the processed Seurat object to a Monocle3 object.
Learn the trajectory graph by fitting a principal graph within each partition.
Select root cells that represent the start of the biological process to order cells along pseudotime.
Plot pseudotime progress on UMAP, coloring by cell‑cycle phase, pseudotime, clusters, or marker‑gene expression.

steps.title: Extract matrix and execute CoGAPS
steps.instruction: Perform non‑negative matrix factorization on variable‑gene expression data.

substeps.instruction: Extract expression data for the top variable genes from the processed Seurat object as a matrix.
Run Coordinated Gene Association in Pattern Sets (CoGAPS) on this matrix using default parameters.

steps.title: Analyze gene expression patterns
steps.instruction: Visualize and test the significance of CoGAPS‑derived patterns.

substeps.instruction: Extract the matrix of sample weights for each pattern learned by CoGAPS.
Visualize patterns on UMAP plots using sample weights to assess association with clusters or phenotypes.
Test the significance of each association with a Kruskal‑Wallis rank‑sum test.
Create a heatmap of sample weights per cell to further evaluate pattern‑cluster relationships.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for interrogating heterogeneous collective migration phenotypes of MDA-MB-231 cells in a 3D collagen matrix. However, this protocol can be used with other cell lines and other culture platforms and is easily adaptable to other biological contexts that can be visually defined. The experimental workflow and timing of the procedures is shown in Figure 1, which depicts the different stages of the Procedure. In broad terms, the Procedure consists of five main sections, which are detailed below.Note: It is important to verify that the biological heterogeneity being studied is not altered through expression of the photoconvertible protein or the photoconversion process. Cells expressing the photoconvertible protein should be compared to wild-type cells to ensure the same modes of heterogeneity exist and at similar frequencies. In addition, to confirm that the photoconversion process does not significantly alter gene expression, a non-labeled population can be compared to the sorted populations through gene expression assays to demonstrate minimal difference. In particular, genes associated with responses to light should not be significantly differentially expressed between labeled and unlabeled populations.Note: Proper controls must also be used to ensure collection of purified photoconverted populations. A non-photoconverted sample exhibiting equivalent biological heterogeneity should be used to gate the baseline fluorescence of the photoconverted channel. To ensure purity of the sample, a strict gate should be applied where all cells collected express higher fluorescence in the photoconverted channel compared to the negative control.
